turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung's face twisted in anger, he scolded O-lan, how could she be so foolish, to think of such things when she was so weak?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung must think of the future, of his son's marriage and his grandchildren

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son spoke up, his voice tinged with a mixture of concern and exasperation, as he said, 'Father, do not scold Mother, she is only thinking of me and my future, and what she wants is for me to be happy and well-settled.'

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: How could she think of such things when her own life was slipping away like sand between his fingers?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung must think of what will become of our son when O-lan is gone, and he must make sure he finds a good wife, a woman who will take care of him and give him sons.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Foolish O-lan, must she think of such things when her own body is weak and her life is slipping away?

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He knows his mother wants him to be happy, and he will not disappoint her, but he must also think of his own future and what he wants, not just what his mother wants for him.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: The eldest son will not find a good wife if Wang Lung does not help him, so Wang Lung must take care of this now, before it is too late.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: How can O-lan ask Wang Lung to think of such things when she is but a shadow of her former self, her body worn down by suffering and pain?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung must see to it that the eldest son finds a good wife, someone who will take care of him and bring him joy, not just someone to share his bed

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son thought of a good wife who would bring joy to his life, and he was eager to please his mother, but he also wanted to start his new life with someone who would be a true partner, not just a companion

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: How can Wang Lung possibly find a good wife for his son when his own wife's life is slipping away from her?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan's eyes narrowed, her voice low and urgent, as she spoke of Wang Lung's duty to find a wife for the eldest son, and soon, or the son would be left with no one to care for him when she was gone.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was worried about his mother's concerns, he told O-lan, and he would surely find a good wife, one who would bring joy to their home, just as she had always done.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung must see to it that the eldest son is married before O-lan is gone, for it is his duty and the way of their family.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid, timid and respectful, spoke up, 'Pardon, honored mother, but perhaps it would be better to consider the young son's feelings and his desire for a true partner, rather than just a companion.'

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: How can Wang Lung think of the eldest son's happiness when O-lan's own time on this earth is coming to an end?

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung's thoughts were consumed by the eldest son's happiness, but his own wife's mortality weighed heavily on his mind, and he wondered how he could consider the son's future when O-lan's own time on this earth was drawing to a close, her frailty and distress a constant reminder of the inevitable.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was glad that his mother and father were thinking of his future, and he hoped to bring joy to their family by finding a good wife.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung must see to it that the eldest son is married, and not just to a companion, but to a woman who will bring him children and care for him when O-lan is no longer here to tend to him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
